validation.notes: Ran from the workspace root with Node v24.14.0; the script prints 'regression: revocation clears cached resources and settings — all assertions passed' and exits 0 in about 0.2s. It imports the real production modules through .prale-eval/subject.mjs (project-trust resolver, SettingsManager, DefaultResourceLoader, package-manager binding) and asserts across module boundaries, with only settings storage, package resolution, extension loading and the UI faked. Covered: (1) headless reload with ask policy and no stored decision denies trust and yields only cli.ts/global.ts with empty project settings and global default model, without persisting a decision; (2) stored approval loads project.ts and project settings, and loader.reload() without a resolver retains the trusted state; (3) revoking a previous approval (stored denial, CLI-style override false, or direct setProjectTrusted(false)) immediately clears cached project settings, falls back to global values, and removes project extensions from the next resolved set while preserving global and CLI resources; (4) the untrusted bootstrap set handed to the resolver already excludes project extensions; (5) documented non-ask paths still work (always approves headlessly, never denies, interactive approval is honoured). Uncaught node:assert/strict assertions only; ordering is promise-driven, no timers, randomness or external services. Mutation check: restoring project-trust.ts, settings-manager.ts or resource-loader.ts one at a time to its faulty baseline makes the script fail with a genuine AssertionError (not a crash, import error or timeout). Limitation: the repository vitest suites and tsc could not be executed because node_modules is absent and installing dependencies is out of scope; the regression script uses only Node built-ins. No temporary files are created (in-memory storage, faked loader/UI), so no cleanup was required.

claims.claim: A headless reload with no stored decision and ask policy denies access instead of granting trust.
Revoking trust immediately discards cached project configuration.
Project extensions leave the next resolved resource set after revocation, while global and CLI resources are preserved.
A reload without a resolver retains the existing trust state.
claims.repair: resource-loader.ts reload() only bootstraps and re-decides when a resolveProjectTrust callback is supplied; settings-manager.ts reload() preserves projectTrusted

claims.claim: A missing UI is never treated as implicit consent and no trust decision is persisted on denial.
claims.repair: packages/coding-agent/src/core/project-trust.ts: denial path returns before any prompt or trust-store write
